subject: Status - BBBC021 reproduced, transfer is the open question
body:
Reproduction is done and it was less painful than expected. On the CellProfiler embeddings, after percentile-matching normalization plus factor analysis, the Wasserstein-corrected representation recovers mechanism-of-action clustering at 0.71 vs 0.52 uncorrected. Deep-network embeddings land in the same neighbourhood. Both within noise of the paper.

The risk is the transfer claim in Anders' kickoff. The imaging case has a clean nuisance variable - the plate - and hundreds of samples per plate. Our text corpus has labeling waves of wildly uneven size, some with 40 documents. The Wasserstein estimate is badly biased at that sample size, and in the first run the correction erased about as much signal as noise: retrieval nDCG moved -0.4 points, i.e. nothing, with wider variance.

Linnea is testing whether pooling small waves into synthetic batches helps. If it doesn't, my honest read is that this is an imaging tool, not a corpus layer.

Umar
